characters_note: Composites, all invented. A character's page in the journal is assembled from every trace tagged "about" them (documents, excerpts, captions, Bertha fragments and echo figures); "closing" appears only when every trace has been found.

characters.name: Margaret Hale, R.N.
characters.notes: Composite. Kept the lamp on all night. Wrote people's names, never numbers.
characters.closing: Margaret Hale worked nights on Ward 3 North for longer than anyone wrote down. She kept the lamp on, she kept the day book in names rather than numbers, and she scratched a promise into the base of a brass bell so that nobody would have to shout. Ring once and I'll come. The ward is dark now, but the lamp is back on the counter, turned toward the hall.

characters.name: Mrs. D.
characters.notes: Composite. Loudest in the choir. Stopped eating in February 1953 and started again in March.
characters.closing: Nobody wrote down what the D stood for. The ward knew her by her voice: loudest in the choir, first to the table when she was eating and last when she wasn't. Through February 1953 she ate nothing worth writing down. On the fourth of March she finished her supper, and the night nurse thought it mattered enough to record. Five days later she was singing.

characters.name: Ida
characters.notes: Composite. Ruth's mother. Sat at the bay window and watched the water.
characters.closing: Ida sat at the bay window. The other women crowded the piano and Ida kept her place on the bench, watching the road along the water for a daughter who said she would come on Sunday. Whether Ruth came, the ward did not record. Ida kept watching.

characters.name: Ruth
characters.notes: Composite. Wrote to her mother promising a Sunday visit.
characters.closing: Ruth is the only person on this page who was never a patient here. She wrote to her mother in a careful hand, promised a Sunday and a blue scarf, and asked her to watch from the window. The letter was kept. That is all the ward knows about Ruth, and it is enough to know she was expected.

characters.name: Dorothy
characters.notes: Composite. Played the day room piano.
characters.closing: Dorothy played. The day book doesn't say whether she had lessons or learned by ear, only that on a snowy afternoon in March 1953 she sat down at the day room piano after lunch and eleven women sang. The hymnal was hers to open.

documents.kicker: Found in Room 2, on the floor
documents.title: Desk lamp
documents.label: Note under the desk lamp
documents.text:
A slip of paper is folded under the base:

"Night girls: leave the lamp ON and turned toward the hall. If somebody wakes up frightened, the first thing they should see is that someone is here.  — M.H."

documents.kicker: Found in the dining room dumbwaiter
documents.title: Ward day book, 1953
documents.text:
Mar. 4  Mrs. D. ate all of her supper. First time since February.

Mar. 9  Snow to the sills. Dorothy played hymns on the day room piano after lunch. Eleven ladies sang.

Mar. 12  Nobody on this ward is a number. Write their names.  — M. Hale, R.N.

documents.kicker: Found in Room 4, by the radiator
documents.title: Brass call bell
documents.label: Scratched into the bell
documents.text:
Someone scratched words into the base with a hairpin:

"RING ONCE & I'LL COME"

documents.label: The station, March 1953
documents.text: March 1953, a little after two in the morning. The lamp is turned toward the hall. Margaret Hale is writing the night report, and somewhere down the corridor, someone is awake. She will hear the bell before it finishes ringing.

documents.kicker: Found in the tunnel, near the collapse
documents.title: Day room hymnal
documents.label: Inside the hymnal's cover
documents.text:
Swollen from the damp, the pages stuck together. Inside the cover, in pencil:

"PROPERTY OF WARD 3 NORTH DAY ROOM. Please return to the piano.  — M.H."

Someone carried it a long way from home.

documents.label: The day room, March 9, 1953
documents.text: March 9, 1953. Snow to the windowsills and the radiator ticking. Eleven ladies crowd around the day room piano, and Mrs. D. sings louder than anyone. At the bay window, Ruth's mother keeps one eye on the water.

documents.kicker: Found on the bench under the bay window
documents.title: A letter from Ruth
documents.label: Ruth's letter
documents.text:
The envelope says Ida, Ward 3 North, in a careful hand. Inside:

"Dear Mother,

I will come on Sunday afternoon, and I will bring the blue scarf you asked for. Watch for me from your window and I will wave from the road.

Your Ruth"
